issues.issue: Did the officer wrongly treat the applicant's never having travelled in Canada or outside China as relevant?
issues.applicant_position: Lack of travel is irrelevant to a self-employed-class visa and was wrongly weighed against him.
issues.respondent_position: Travel and uniqueness were part of the business-plan adequacy assessment, so relevant.
issues.result_quote: The fact that the applicant has never travelled to Canada or outside China is indeed irrelevant

issues.issue: Did the officer wrongly require the applicant to show uniqueness in his profession?
issues.applicant_position: Requiring uniqueness among graphic designers is an unsupported burden the Act and Regulations do not impose.
issues.respondent_position: Uniqueness was part of the business-plan adequacy assessment, so relevant.
issues.result_quote: nothing in the Act or Regulations imposes such a high burden on an applicant for a visa in the self-employed class

issues.issue: Should the visa refusal be set aside and the application sent to another officer?
issues.applicant_position: Reliance on irrelevant factors means the refusal must be set aside.
issues.respondent_position: Factors were part of the business-plan assessment, so no reason to interfere with the decision.
issues.result_quote: I find that the appropriate solution in the circumstances is to return the case to another visa officer for reconsideration
